messages.subject: Shared random effects - estimates
parts:
Hi everyone, 
I am trying to jointly model 2 outcomes with shared random effects (u,v) and extra random terms for the 2nd outcome (u2+v2) 
 Y ~ Poisson(r*pop)
log(r1) = intercept1 + u + v 
log(r2) = intercept2 + u + v +u2 +v2

I run the code as follows:

n <- nrow(data)
###Response
Y <- matrix(NA, ncol = 2, nrow = 2 * n)
Y[1:n, 1] <- data$y1
Y[n + 1:n, 2] <- data$y2
###Intercept
Inter <- matrix(NA, nrow = 2 * n, ncol = 2)
Inter[1:n, 1] <- 1
Inter[n + 1:n, 2] <- 1
###offset
OS<- c(log(data$pop1),log(data$pop2))
###shared random terms
ID.shared1=c(data$ID,rep(NA,n))
ID.shared2=c(rep(NA,n),data$ID)
# extra random terms for y2 
ID.2=c(rep(NA, n),data$ID)

#Model fit
fit.formula <- Y ~ 0 + Inter + offset(OS) +f(ID.shared1, model = "bym",graph=Wmat)+
  f(ID.shared2,copy = 'ID.shared1', model = "bym",graph=Wmat)+f(ID.2, model = "bym",graph=Wmat)

fit2FL <- inla(fit.formula, family = c("poisson", "poisson"),
                      data = list(Y = Y, Inter = Inter,OS=OS, ID.shared1=ID.shared1,
                                  ID.shared2=ID.shared2,ID.2=ID.2),
                      control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
                      control.compute = list(config=T),
                      control.inla=list(strategy="gaussian"))

I want to get estimates for the random terms so I use "summary.random". Based on the way I defined them, I thought that I will only get estimates for the first n rows of ID.shared1, the last n rows of ID.shared2 and the last n rows of ID.2. The rest elements would be blank. Nevertheless, I get estimates for all 2*n rows of each random term. 

Is this something to expect or I made a mistake while defining the model?

Thank very much in advance!

Best regards,
Hanah.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Shared random effects - estimates
parts:
the 'copy' will copy the whole model , hence you'll get estimate of all
of them even if they are not observed.


--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org
